title: Perfectness, cardinality, dual cubicles, and their order
notes: All cubicles are Boolean algebras with \(2^n\) elements, the lower ones are dual, and ``all are ordered''. No completeness conjecture is stated.
statement: For \(r\ge4\), each \(B^+(\ell)\) and its lattice-dual \(B^-(\ell)\) has \(2^r\) perfect elements. If \(\ell<m\), every element of \(B^+(\ell)\) lies above every element of \(B^+(m)\); duality reverses this for lower cubicles. The 1974 source proves comparison of arbitrary lower and upper cubicles after applying every linear representation, while explicitly distinguishing this from the corresponding unproved-at-that-time literal inequality in \(D^r\).
reconstruction: Replace the unexplained \(n\) by the number \(r\) of generators. ``Ordered'' cannot mean that a Boolean cubicle is a total order. The source's separate conjecture that these exhaust all perfect elements is absent from these notes and is not added to this year's problem list.
fate: \citet[\S1.3, pp.~4--5, and main theorem]{gelfandponomarev1974modular} supplies exactly these distinctions.
present_status: As of November 2026: The stated perfectness/cardinality theorem is established. The ambiguous short ordering phrase does not determine a further unresolved claim; no C/D classification is warranted.

title: Complete irreducibility over the rational prime field
notes: In characteristic zero a representation is completely irreducible if its image is isomorphic to \(L(\mathbb Q^n)\), or projective geometry \(P(n-1,\mathbb Q)\).
statement: Let \(V\) be finite dimensional over a characteristic-zero field \(F\). In Gelfand--Ponomarev's terminology, \(\rho:L\to L(V)\) is completely irreducible when its image lattice is isomorphic to the full lattice of rational linear subspaces of a finite-dimensional \(\mathbb Q\)-space (equivalently, the associated rational projective geometry, including its extremal subspaces). This is stronger than indecomposability and is not the assertion \(\rho(L)=L(V,F)\).
reconstruction: The rational prime field is intentional even when the target field is larger. The notebook gives a definition, not the paper's full classification of the completely irreducible representations.
fate: Exact definition in \citet[\S1.4]{gelfandponomarev1974modular}.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established specialized terminology; its intended field must be retained.

title: Virasoro, the Witt quotient, and a central-sign convention
notes: The bracket is \([e_i,e_j]=(j-i)e_{i+j}+\delta_{i,-j}(i^3-i)C/12\); the quotient by the center is called the algebra of vector fields on the circle. Positive-index modes are creators.
statement: Over \(\mathbb C\), use \([L_m,L_n]=(m-n)L_{m+n}+\delta_{m,-n}(m^3-m)c/12\), with \(c\) central. The quotient is the Witt algebra of Laurent-polynomial vector fields, with \(L_m=-z^{m+1}\partial_z\). The notebook's bracket is isomorphic by \(e_i=L_{-i}\), \(C=-c\). Its algebraic direct sum is not the Fr\'echet Lie algebra of all smooth vector fields on the circle.
reconstruction: This change of indices also changes the sign of the central generator. The Kac polynomial and positive Sugawara central charge on the next pages use the usual \(c\); they cannot be compared with the first bracket without this conversion. The central extension itself is legitimate. Editorial reversal-of-modes and central-sign computation \oursComputed.
fate: The exact conventions and Verma-module setup can be checked in \citet[\S3.1]{feiginfuchs1982invariant}, received September 1981 and published in 1982.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established definition; a convention mismatch is recorded without treating the existence of the algebra as an open problem.

title: Verma modules and their grading
notes: A vacuum satisfies \(e_0v=hv\), \(Cv=cv\), and \(e_{-i}v=0\) for \(i>0\). Dixmier and Bernstein--Gelfand--Gelfand are mentioned; the category name reads \ru{Оре}.
statement: In the usual convention, let \(M(h,c)=U(\mathrm{Vir})\otimes_{U(\mathfrak b)}\mathbb C_{h,c}\), where \(\mathfrak b\) is spanned by \(L_n\) for \(n\ge0\) and the central generator, \(L_nv=0\) for \(n>0\), \(L_0v=hv\), and the center acts by \(c\). For arbitrary \(h,c\in\mathbb C\), the PBW basis consists of \(L_{-\lambda_1}\cdots L_{-\lambda_s}v\) with \(\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_s>0\); grade \(N\) has dimension the partition number \(p(N)\).
reconstruction: The central eigenvalue is converted as in the preceding item. No integrability or unitarity assumption belongs to the general Verma module. The uncertain category word is not silently expanded into a particular title or paper.
fate: The construction and grading occur in \citet[\S3.1]{feiginfuchs1982invariant}. The notebook's short bibliography does not identify the two BGG papers uniquely.
present_status: As of November 2026: Known highest-weight representation theory. The historical reading uncertainty is narrower than the fully identifiable mathematical construction.

title: The reducibility criterion and the miscopied Kac polynomial
notes: The question is when \(M_{h,c}\) is reducible. The displayed \(\Phi_{rs}\) has final coefficient \(1/2\), followed by an if-and-only-if statement attributed to Feigin and Fuchs.
statement: For the usual Virasoro bracket, put \(c(t)=13-6(t+t^{-1})\) and \(h_{r,s}(t)=((rt-s)^2-(t-1)^2)/(4t)\), where \(t\in\mathbb C^\times\) and \(r,s\ge1\) are integers. Then \(M(h,c)\) is reducible exactly when \(c=c(t)\), \(h=h_{r,s}(t)\) for some such data. Equivalently some \(\Phi_{rs}(h,c)\) vanishes, with \(\Phi_{rs}=\prod_{j\in\{r,s\}}[h+(c-13)(j^2-1)/24+(rs-1)/2]+(r^2-s^2)^2/16\); the product uses both entries, even if \(r=s\).
reconstruction: The manuscript visibly has \(1/2\), whereas the identified paper has \(1/16\). The difference is not a harmless scalar multiple of the polynomial. For example, at \(c=1,r=1,s=2\) the correct factor is \((h-1/4)^2\). The central-sign conversion from the first item is also required. Editorial substitution \(c=1,r=1,s=2\) \oursComputed; the corrected coefficient itself is read in Feigin--Fuchs.
fate: \citet[\S3.2, Thm.~3.1 and its corollary, printed pp.~58--59]{feiginfuchs1982invariant} gives the determinant and reducibility result. This repeats problem GP-1982-03, occurrence 1982-566.7; publication preceded this talk by three years.
present_status: As of November 2026: Solved before the seminar. The theorem is E; its displayed polynomial is false as written.

title: Singular vectors and the first singular grade
notes: A reducible Verma module contains a non-vacuum vector killed by all annihilation modes, and its level is asserted to be \(rs\).
statement: Every nonzero proper submodule of a Virasoro Verma module contains a homogeneous vector of positive grade killed by all \(L_n\), \(n>0\): choose its least occupied grade. If \(M(h,c)\) is reducible, its first such grade is \(\min\{rs:\Phi_{rs}(h,c)=0\}\). At a point on just one reducibility component this is the corresponding product \(rs\). Intersections require specifying which pair or which singular vector is meant.
reconstruction: The elementary least-grade argument proves existence but does not by itself compute the grade. The determinant formula supplies the minimum. It is not legitimate to select an arbitrary pair among several vanishing factors and call its product the first level. Editorial least-grade proof of singular-vector existence \ours; computation of the first grade uses the published determinant theorem.
fate: \citet[\S3.2, corollary to Thm.~3.1]{feiginfuchs1982invariant} explicitly gives the existence criterion for a singular vector of degree at most a prescribed integer.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established before 1985, with the collision qualification made explicit. It belongs to the same earlier indexed problem.

title: Laurent vector fields, infinite matrices, and Fock realizations
notes: The first proof mechanism maps the Witt quotient into \(gl_\infty\), \(O_\infty\), or \(sp_\infty\), then uses suitable representations.
statement: Laurent-polynomial vector fields act by Lie derivative on tensor densities. On Laurent half-densities the pairing \(\operatorname{Res}(fg\,dz)\) is symmetric, invariant, and nondegenerate. On \(\mathbb C[z,z^{-1}]/\mathbb C\), the pairing \(\operatorname{Res}(f\,dg)\) is alternating, invariant, and nondegenerate. In Laurent bases these actions have finitely many nonzero diagonals, not finitely many nonzero entries. Passing to a polarized wedge or spin representation requires its central extension and a specified completion.
reconstruction: These explicit models explain the three classical-algebra labels without falsely embedding Witt in the finitary matrix algebra. They are an editorial reconstruction of a one-line construction, not three complete theorems asserted in the notes. Editorial residue-pairing reconstruction of the indicated classical-algebra models \ours; the Fock constructions are prior literature.
fate: The relevant semi-infinite wedge mechanism is used in \citet[\S4]{feiginfuchs1982invariant}. Kac--Peterson's 1981 spin and wedge paper is an earlier primary reference identified in that paper; only its author-maintained metadata was checked here \citep{kacpeterson1981spin}.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established representation-theoretic method. The notebook does not specify enough completion data to identify every indicated model exactly.

title: The affine current algebra and Gelfand's intervention
notes: A simple finite-dimensional \(\mathfrak g\) is replaced by a one-dimensional extension of its current algebra. Gelfand explains currents as matrix functions on the circle. A Killing form and dual root/Cartan bases are chosen.
statement: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra, with invariant form \(B\) normalized so long roots have squared length 2. Its untwisted affine algebra without the degree derivation is \(\widehat{\mathfrak g}=\mathfrak g[z,z^{-1}]\oplus\mathbb C K\), with \([xz^m,yz^n]=[x,y]z^{m+n}+m\delta_{m,-n}B(x,y)K\). A level-\(k\) module has \(K=k\,\mathrm{id}\). The basis used in the quadratic construction is dual with respect to this same form.
reconstruction: The algebraic loop algebra suffices for the formulas. Smooth loops require a topological completion. The normalized form is generally a scalar multiple of the raw Killing form; changing it changes the numerical level and the denominator involving the dual Coxeter number.
fate: The current-algebra setup appears in \citet[p.~132, eq.~(10)]{kent1985unitary}; the paper is a contemporary account of the already circulating Sugawara and coset constructions.
present_status: As of November 2026: Known construction. Gelfand's explanatory intervention is preserved without treating matrix-valued smooth functions and algebraic Laurent currents as identical categories.
speaker: B. L. Feigin; I. M. Gelfand (intervention)

title: Sugawara operators, normal ordering, and the noncritical level
notes: The quadratic sums \(S(m)\) are called elements of the enveloping algebra; one inner sum has \(r\in\Delta\). The notes give their commutator and divide by \(2(g+k)\).
statement: On a restricted level-\(k\) \(\widehat{\mathfrak g}\)-module, each vector is killed by \(xz^m\) for sufficiently large positive \(m\). If \(k\ne-h^\vee\), the normally ordered operators \(L_n=[2(k+h^\vee)]^{-1}\sum_a\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}:J^a_mJ_{a,n-m}:\) are well defined on each vector and satisfy the Virasoro relations with \(c=k\dim\mathfrak g/(k+h^\vee)\), as well as \([L_n,J^a_m]=-mJ^a_{n+m}\). Normal ordering places annihilation modes to the right; the zero-mode convention is fixed consistently with the quadratic Casimir.
reconstruction: The root sum is over \(\alpha\in\Delta\), but both mode sums are over \(\mathbb Z\). The infinite quadratic expression lies in a suitable completion, or defines operators on a restricted module, not in the ordinary finite-sum enveloping algebra. At the critical level the displayed division is undefined. Indices and the central sign are converted to the usual convention. Editorial quadratic-scaling and central-sign check \oursComputed; the Sugawara theorem itself is from the cited source.
fate: \citet[p.~133, eqs.~(15)--(17)]{kent1985unitary} gives the Sugawara formula and charge. Multiplication by \(2(k+h^\vee)\) recovers the noncentral scaling of the quadratic commutator. Reversing mode indices also reverses the central sign; the notebook's displayed positive central term and later standard positive charge are not one consistent convention.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established construction. The missing denominator hypothesis, summation domain, completion, and form normalization are essential mathematical qualifications.

title: The affine sl2 example and the spin/Dynkin-label mismatch
notes: For \(\widehat{sl}_2\), the notes put \(k=k_1+k_2\), \(c=3k/(k+2)\), and \(h=k_1(k_1+1)/(k+2)\).
statement: For a highest-weight \(\widehat{sl}_2\)-module of level \(k\ne-2\), let \(\ell\) denote the finite \(sl_2\) highest weight in Dynkin-label normalization. Then the Sugawara highest weight is \(h=\ell(\ell+2)/(4(k+2))\) and \(c=3k/(k+2)\). If \(j=\ell/2\) is the spin, this becomes \(h=j(j+1)/(k+2)\). Affine Dynkin labels satisfy \(\lambda_0+\lambda_1=k\), with \(\ell=\lambda_1\).
reconstruction: The notebook uses \(k_1\) both as an affine label contributing with coefficient one to \(k\) and as a spin. Those are different normalizations. Neither integrality nor unitarity is needed for this formal highest-weight formula; integrable unitary modules further have \(k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), \(0\le\ell\le k\). Editorial spin-to-Dynkin-label conversion \oursComputed.
fate: The \(SU(2)\) charge and highest-weight formulas are stated in \citet[p.~133]{kent1985unitary}, immediately following the Sugawara construction.
present_status: As of November 2026: A standard example with a genuine normalization mismatch in its paired formulas.

title: The coset difference commutes with the subalgebra currents
notes: For \(\mathfrak g\supset\mathfrak g_1\), subtract the two Sugawara actions. The difference is Virasoro, commutes with \(\widehat{\mathfrak g}_i\), and has the difference of the central charges.
statement: Let \(\mathfrak h\subset\mathfrak g\) be complex simple Lie algebras, with embedding index \(I\) in the normalized invariant forms. On a restricted level-\(k\) \(\widehat{\mathfrak g}\)-module, the induced \(\widehat{\mathfrak h}\)-level is \(Ik\). Assume \(k+h^\vee_{\mathfrak g}\ne0\) and \(Ik+h^\vee_{\mathfrak h}\ne0\). Then \(L_n^{\mathrm{coset}}=L_n^{\mathfrak g}-L_n^{\mathfrak h}\) commutes with all \(\widehat{\mathfrak h}\) currents and satisfies Virasoro with \(c_{\mathrm{coset}}=k\dim\mathfrak g/(k+h^\vee_{\mathfrak g})-Ik\dim\mathfrak h/(Ik+h^\vee_{\mathfrak h})\).
reconstruction: The subscript is \(1\), not the running mode index \(i\). The embedding index and both noncritical conditions are supplied. The charge here is a scalar on the fixed-level module; subtracting abstract central generators without fixing levels is not this statement.
fate: \citet[pp.~133--134, eqs.~(18)--(20)]{kent1985unitary} states the construction, commutation, and charge difference, as an account of the Goddard--Kent--Olive work.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established by 1985. The seminar is an exposition of the coset mechanism, not an unattributed new open problem.

title: The Selberg integral: exponent and chamber normalization
notes: The first integral has a Vandermonde power \(\rho\), unspecified product ranges, and limits 0 and 1. Its gamma product starts with \(\prod_{i=1}^m\Gamma(i\rho)/\Gamma(\rho)\). It is called a special case of Fateev--Dotsenko.
statement: For \(m\ge1\), real \(\alpha,\beta>-1\) and \(\rho>0\), the integral over \(0<t_1<\cdots<t_m<1\) of \(\prod_{i<j}(t_j-t_i)^{2\rho}\prod_i t_i^\alpha(1-t_i)^\beta\,dt_1\cdots dt_m\) equals exactly the gamma product printed in (17). The symmetric integral over \([0,1]^m\), with \(|t_i-t_j|^{2\rho}\), is \(m!\) times that product. Meromorphic continuation is a later statement about the resulting functions of the exponents, not unconditional convergence of the original integral.
reconstruction: These are sufficient convergence hypotheses. The Vandermonde exponent is doubled, and an ordered chamber is specified to match the printed right side; alternatively keep the cube and multiply that side by \(m!\). No branch ambiguity remains under the displayed real hypotheses. Editorial chamber-to-cube normalization check \oursComputed; the Selberg evaluation is classical.
fate: This is Selberg's classical integral, announced in 1941 and proved in 1944; see the authors' derivation and historical account in \citet[eqs.~(1.1)--(1.2) and pp.~1--2]{forresterwarnaar2008selberg}. Dotsenko--Fateev's use is a later conformal-field-theory application, not its origin.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established well before the seminar; the exact notebook formula fails without correcting its exponent and integration convention.

title: Two screening charges and the missing integration cycle
notes: The displayed integral has \(n\) charges \(\alpha_+\), \(m\) charges \(\alpha_-\), \(\alpha_+\alpha_-=-2\), same-species powers \(\alpha_\pm^2\), mixed power \(-2\), and powers of \(t_i\) and \(z-t_i\). One product ends at \(m+1\) and the differentials end at \(dt_n\).
statement: In a chiral free-boson normalization with charge weight \(\Delta(q)=q(q-2q_0)/2\), choose screening charges solving \(\Delta(\alpha_\pm)=1\); then \(\alpha_++\alpha_-=2q_0\) and \(\alpha_+\alpha_-=-2\). For nonnegative integers \(n,m\), impose sphere charge neutrality \(\sum_aq_a+n\alpha_++m\alpha_-=2q_0\), including the charge at infinity. Wick contractions produce pair factors with exponents equal to charge products. Integrating the screening variables over compatible complex contours or twisted cycles gives chiral blocks, when those integrals converge or have a specified regularization. The mixed range is \(1\le u\le n<n+1\le v\le n+m\), and all \(n+m\) differentials are required.
reconstruction: The charge convention is specified explicitly; Dotsenko--Fateev also use a rescaled convention. For four insertions fixed at \(0,z,1,\infty\), powers of \(1-t_i\), generally different species-dependent external-charge powers, branch choices, and cycles must also be supplied. A common real cube with both species present is not an absolutely convergent integral across the mixed double poles. The missing external charges cannot be uniquely recovered from this page. Editorial mixed-double-pole divergence check \ours; the contour construction is due to Dotsenko--Fateev.
fate: \citet[\S3, especially eqs.~(3.30)--(3.36)]{dotsenkofateev1984conformal} constructs screening integrals and discusses their contours; the paper was received 17 April 1984 and published in 1984.
present_status: As of November 2026: An identifiable established method; the literal integral is incomplete and its ordinary-real-integral interpretation is false.

title: Four-point blocks depend on a cross-ratio
notes: The integral is first called a two-point correlation function and then a four-point function depending on the cross-ratio \(z\).
statement: For four distinct points on \(\mathbb P^1\), projective transformations fix three to \(0,1,\infty\) and leave one complex cross-ratio \(z\). Chiral four-point conformal blocks may therefore have one nontrivial complex argument. A physical single-valued nonchiral correlation is an appropriate sesquilinear combination of such blocks and their antiholomorphic partners; a chiral contour integral alone is not automatically that correlation.
reconstruction: The lower four-point statement resolves the internal two-/four-point mismatch. A two-point function on the sphere has no independent cross-ratio. The distinction between a block and a full correlation is added because the notebook uses the latter term indiscriminately.
fate: \citet[\S3, eqs.~(3.39)--(3.42), and \S4]{dotsenkofateev1984conformal} explicitly fixes the four points and combines the solutions.
present_status: As of November 2026: Known conformal covariance and block construction; the first label is a faithful mathematical slip.

title: Analytic continuation in the number of screenings
notes: The ``real'' correlation functions are said to be analytic continuations of the integral formulas to complex \(n,m\).
statement: A sequence of integrals defined only for \((n,m)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^2\) does not by itself determine a unique holomorphic or meromorphic function of two complex variables. If one continuation \(F(n,m)\) exists, then \(F(n,m)+\sin(\pi n)H(n,m)\) has the same values on every integer pair for any holomorphic \(H\). A well-posed continuation claim therefore needs a target class, singularity and growth conditions, functional equations, or an independently defined correlation function.
reconstruction: No such selection principle is stated. This is not the familiar analytic continuation of the Selberg integral in its continuous exponents: there the integral is first defined on an open parameter domain. The displayed ambiguity is an elementary editorial check. Editorial nonuniqueness example using \(\sin(\pi n)\) \ours.
fate: The source screening construction is \citet[\S3]{dotsenkofateev1984conformal}. For comparison, \citet[pp.~1--2]{forresterwarnaar2008selberg} carefully invokes a growth theorem in a continuation argument; neither source establishes the notebook's unrestricted two-integer-variable assertion.
present_status: As of November 2026: Insufficiently formulated (F), not an open problem licensed by the vague claim. No universal continuation theorem is asserted here.

title: Topology of Grassmannian configuration strata
notes: For \(E\in G(n,m)\), the notes set \(\tau_E=(P_Ee_1,\ldots,P_Ee_n)\) and ask for the topology of the stratum with prescribed combinatorial type.
statement: Fix labels and a rank-\(m\) incidence or oriented-matroid type \(\mathcal M\) on \(n\) elements. Study the locus of \(m\)-planes whose coordinate projections realize \(\mathcal M\). The oriented version fixes signs of maximal minors after an orientation is chosen; the unoriented version fixes ranks of subsets. These are different stratifications.
reconstruction: The notebook does not choose between incidence data, an oriented matroid, and a face lattice. The statement makes these alternatives explicit rather than identifying their spaces.
fate: Configuration varieties and their normalized forms were already treated in \citet[definitions and Theorems~1--3]{mnev1985varieties}, published in 1985 from a manuscript received in July 1984. The broader question is therefore expository here, although its fixed-dimensional polytope variant below is not settled by that paper.
present_status: As of November 2026, universality rules out a general simple classification of these strata. Exact topology requires specifying the combinatorial data and normalization.

title: Every polytope type as an orthogonal projection of a simplex
notes: The exercise asks to obtain combinatorially every \(m\)-dimensional convex polytope with \(n\) vertices by projecting \(S=\operatorname{conv}(e_1,\ldots,e_n)\subset\mathbb R^n\) to an \(m\)-plane.
statement: If \(Q=\operatorname{conv}(v_1,\ldots,v_n)\subset\mathbb R^m\) is full-dimensional, let \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) have columns \(v_i\), and put \(E=(\ker A)^\perp\). Then \(A|_E\) is invertible and \(A=(A|_E)P_E\). Thus \(Q\) is linearly isomorphic to \(P_E S\), so their labelled face lattices agree.
reconstruction: Full-dimensionality ensures that \(A\) has rank \(m\). The proof supplies the omitted linear isomorphism; the projected vertices need not equal the given numerical coordinates. \ours\ The factorization through \((\ker A)^\perp\) is the elementary proof supplied here; no universality assertion is being proved by it.
fate: This is an elementary linear-algebra verification of the notebook exercise; it does not require a new universality theorem. The configuration/Grassmannian framework is contemporary with \citet[p.~1312]{mnev1985varieties}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Isotopy of matrices with prescribed determinant signs
notes: Two \(3\times n\) matrices \(x,x'\) have all minors nonzero with the same signs. Can one join them through matrices in the same class?
statement: For a realizable uniform rank-three chirotope \(\chi\), is the space \(\{A\in\mathbb R^{3\times n}:\operatorname{sign}\det A_I=\chi(I)\text{ for every }I\in\binom{[n]}3\}\) path connected? With an oriented basis fixed, this is the corresponding normalized realization-space question.
reconstruction: Maximal \(3\times3\) minors are intended in the oriented-matroid interpretation. Literally imposing signs of minors of every size is an additional condition not identified by these references.
fate: The general negative answer follows from rank-three universality already announced by \citet[Theorem~3]{mnev1985varieties}; the later complete uniform formulation is recorded in \citet[Theorem~1(iii)]{adiprasitopadrol2017universality}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the general isotopy assertion is false; realization spaces may be disconnected and have much more complicated topology.

title: The small-configuration bound
notes: The first answer recorded is \(n\leq7\Rightarrow\) a path exists.
statement: For every realizable rank-three oriented matroid on at most seven labelled elements, its normalized realization space is path connected. The uniform version gives the positive answer to the preceding question.
fate: \citet[introduction, p.~287]{tsukamoto2013disconnected} records the stronger established bound of fewer than nine elements, citing the classical small-configuration literature. This verifies the notebook inequality but does not identify its precise historical source.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated bound is valid and not optimal as a general small-size assertion.

title: The nineteen-column counterexample attributed to Mnëv
notes: The notes state \(n=19\Rightarrow\) no path, with N.~E.~Mn\"ev named.
statement: There should exist two realizations of a single uniform rank-three oriented matroid on nineteen labelled elements lying in distinct path components of its realization space.
reconstruction: The formulation assumes that ``all minors'' means maximal minors. A later smaller nonuniform example does not verify this exact claim.
fate: The qualitative counterexample is compatible with Mn\"ev universality, but the exact nineteen-element construction and its uniformity were not located in the opened primary texts. \citet[Theorem~1.3]{tsukamoto2013disconnected} constructs thirteen-element disconnected rank-three spaces with prescribed collinearities; these are not substitutes for the notebook's nonzero-minor assertion.
present_status: As of November 2026, the general phenomenon is established; the notebook's exact numerical example remains an unresolved identification in this companion.

title: Universality for real configuration spaces
notes: The topology can be that of any real algebraic variety.
statement: Every primary basic semialgebraic set defined over \(\mathbb Z\) is stably equivalent to a realization space of a rank-three oriented matroid. For an open such set, the oriented matroid may be chosen uniform. In particular these spaces realize arbitrary finite simplicial-complex homotopy types; equality or homeomorphism to an arbitrary variety is not asserted.
reconstruction: Stable equivalence, integral defining equations and the uniform/open restriction replace the notebook's informal universal quantifier. These qualifications carry arithmetic information beyond homotopy type.
fate: \citet[Theorem~3]{mnev1985varieties} announced the open-set version before the seminar. The standard stable-equivalence formulation and the open/uniform qualification are stated in \citet[Theorem~1]{adiprasitopadrol2017universality}; the latter first circulated in February 2014, appeared online in May 2016, and was printed in 2017.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: A complex analogue of convexity
notes: Over \(\mathbb C\), the analogue is said to be computing \(\pi_1\); the notes then ask what the convex analogue over \(\mathbb C\) is.
statement: Two prompts are recorded: determine fundamental groups of suitably defined complex configuration strata, and identify an appropriate complex counterpart of real convex-polytopal realization spaces. No category of complex convex objects or equivalence relation is specified.
fate: The real universality statements in \citet{mnev1985varieties} do not select a unique complex problem. Searches for complex configuration varieties and realization spaces did not identify an exact result matching both prompts.
present_status: As of November 2026, no precise open problem is extracted: choosing a complex analogue would itself be an editorial addition.

title: Steinitz characterization of three-dimensional polytope graphs
notes: Steinitz's theorem is cited as characterizing the one-dimensional skeleton of a convex polytope in \(\mathbb R^3\).
statement: A finite simple graph is the graph of a convex three-dimensional polytope if and only if it is planar and three-vertex-connected.
fate: \citet[section~2]{richtergebertziegler1995realization} restates the classical theorem and dates the original result to Steinitz, 1922. The theorem predates this seminar by decades.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Contractibility of normalized three-polytope realization spaces
notes: A ``corollary'' says that the space of three-polytopes of a fixed combinatorial type is contractible.
statement: For a realizable labelled three-polytope type, its realization space after fixing an affine basis is contractible; a standard normalized realization-space model is an open ball. The unnormalized collection of all vertex coordinates is not generally contractible.
reconstruction: An affine basis and orientation component must be specified. This does not follow merely from the graph characterization without the stronger realization-space form of Steinitz's theorem.
fate: \citet[section~2, Steinitz theorem]{richtergebertziegler1995realization} gives the normalized open-ball assertion. \citet[p.~1312]{mnev1985varieties} explicitly describes orientation components in an unnormalized model, showing why the normalization cannot be omitted.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Universality for simplicial four-polytope realization spaces
notes: In \(\mathbb R^4\), even simplicial polytopes are said to have \ru{более или менее любой} (``more or less any'') topology for a fixed combinatorial type.
statement: A precise homotopy interpretation would ask: for every nonempty finite simplicial complex \(K\), is there a labelled simplicial four-polytope whose appropriately normalized realization space is homotopy equivalent to \(K\)? The notebook neither specifies this equivalence nor supplies exact quantifiers. A stronger literature conjecture asks for stable equivalence to every nonempty open primary basic semialgebraic set, and even requires the four-polytope to be neighborly.
reconstruction: The displayed homotopy question is an editorial sharpening of the hedge, not a verbatim conjecture attributed to Vershik. Stable-equivalence and homotopy versions must remain separate. Adiprasito--Padrol use a homogenized cone-realization model modulo \(\mathrm{GL}_{d+1}(\mathbb R)\), whereas the bounded proof here fixes an affine frame and a stacking history; their normalizations are not silently identified.
fate: General four-polytope universality was proved in work of 1994 and published by \citet[Main Theorem]{richtergebertziegler1995realization} in 1995. \citet[Theorem~2]{adiprasitopadrol2017universality}, circulated in 2014, published online in 2016 and printed in 2017, proves simplicial/neighborly universality with dimension growing as \(2n-4\); their Conjecture~4 retains dimension four and additionally requires neighborliness. These are distinct results. Adiprasito--Padrol explicitly judge the earlier simplicial proof incomplete and supply its missing argument; the 1985 announcement is not itself a fully checked proof of that part.
present_status: As of November 2026, no resolution of fixed-dimensional simplicial universality was found in this bounded search. The latest opened source explicitly recording the constant-dimension simplicial problem as open is the 2024 compendium, entries CG68--CG69. The chapter proves only a bounded contractibility result for fixed sequences of facet stackings.
worth: Worth developing in bounded families: explicit insertion fibers distinguish tractable history-compatible spaces from the unresolved universal quantifier.

title: Fields of polytopes in tangent spaces
notes: The stated task is to construct a field of polytopes, one in every tangent space of a manifold; a classification problem is mentioned.
statement: For a smooth manifold \(M\), one could prescribe a convex-polytope type \(P\) and ask for a continuous section of the bundle of copies of \(P\) inside \(TM\), then classify such sections up to a specified equivalence. The notebook does not prescribe regularity, a type, or equivalence.
reconstruction: The associated-bundle formulation is a possible modern interpretation only.
fate: \citet[bibliography, item~6]{mnev1985varieties} points to Vershik--Chernyakov's 1982 work on fields of cones as a nearby motivation. This is a lead, not a verified solution of the notebook's classification programme.
present_status: As of November 2026, the recorded programme is too broad to assign a definite unresolved theorem or a new problem-index identifier.

title: Geometric lattices and finite matroids
notes: A geometric lattice is described as semimodular and ``finite'', with a parenthesis saying that every element is a finite join of atoms.
statement: A finite lattice is geometric when it is atomistic and upper semimodular. Atomistic means every element is a join of atoms; finiteness and atomisticity are separate requirements. The lattice of flats of a finite simple matroid is geometric, and conversely every finite geometric lattice arises this way.
fate: This is classical matroid theory, not a new definition in 1985. \citet[sections~1--2]{oxleybriefly} provides a modern author exposition of the underlying finite-matroid definitions; the notebook's conflation is corrected explicitly.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Representability of a geometric lattice by a vector configuration
notes: After ``configuration --- geometric lattice'', the converse question asks when a geometric lattice is given by a configuration.
statement: Given a finite geometric lattice \(L\) and a specified field \(F\), does there exist a finite vector configuration over \(F\) whose lattice of flats is isomorphic to \(L\)? For \(F=\mathbb R\), prescribed ranks can be expressed by vanishing minors and nonvanishing minors, producing a finite semialgebraic feasibility problem.
reconstruction: The field is supplied explicitly. This matroid representation problem is not equivalent to arbitrary join-preserving embeddings of the same lattice into a subspace lattice.
fate: The field dependence is fundamental in classical representability; see \citet[section~4, Theorem~4.1]{oxleybriefly}. The semialgebraic encoding places real representability in the setting of \citet{mnev1985varieties}; it is not a simple combinatorial criterion.
present_status: As of November 2026, individual finite real instances are decidable by real quantifier elimination, while universality explains their potential complexity.

title: The Fano configuration and characteristic two
notes: The seven-point diagram is called the Fano configuration and declared unrealizable over \(\mathbb R\) or \(\mathbb Z\). The scan shows only six of the seven Fano lines.
statement: The Fano matroid \(F_7\) is representable over a field \(F\) exactly when \(\operatorname{char}F=2\). A representation in characteristic two uses the seven nonzero columns of \(\mathbb F_2^3\). No real matrix has exactly its rank incidences; consequently no integer matrix does either.
reconstruction: The named Fano matroid supplies the missing seventh line, but no absent stroke is restored to the manuscript diagram. The characteristic claim is valid for the named object, not for every seven-point drawing with those six lines.
fate: \citet[Theorem~4.1]{oxleybriefly} states the exact characteristic criterion. The result is classical and predates the talk.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Faithful join representations and an unresolved subspace example
notes: A faithful representation \(a:\Gamma\to\mathcal L(F^n)\) is required to preserve strict order and suprema. The following question-marked fragment mentions \(m=4\), \(E,F\), and \(\mathbb R^6\).
statement: An injective join-semilattice map satisfies \(a(x\vee y)=a(x)+a(y)\) and preserves strict order. It need not preserve meets unless that is imposed separately. The fragment involving four-dimensional subspaces of \(\mathbb R^6\) does not determine a particular lattice or a theorem.
fate: \citet[section~1]{gelfandponomarev1974modular} is a genuine pre-1985 source on representations of modular lattices, but the stated join-only definition and the incomplete dimensional fragment do not identify one of its theorems.
present_status: As of November 2026, the definition is interpretable; the intended four-dimensional example and claimed representability remain unidentified.

title: Representability and systems of algebraic inequalities
notes: The notes identify the realization task with solving a system of algebraic inequalities.
statement: For a fixed finite real vector-configuration type, rank constraints can be written as polynomial equalities and strict nonvanishing conditions on minors. Conversely, real configuration realization problems are universal for suitable primary basic semialgebraic sets up to stable equivalence. An arbitrary faithful join embedding of a lattice is a different representation notion and is not covered without further specifications.
reconstruction: The forward encoding and the converse universality statement are separated. Strict inequalities, equations and the equivalence relation cannot all be suppressed.
fate: The universality direction is already present in \citet[Theorem~3]{mnev1985varieties}; \citet[Theorem~1]{adiprasitopadrol2017universality} gives the modern precise formulation.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Gelfand on lattices and their representation theory
notes: Gelfand names Dedekind, Kurosh, Ore, von Neumann, and work with Ponomarev in discussing structures/lattices.
statement: The intervention situates the representation of lattices by subspaces within an older algebraic programme. It contains no further explicitly stated classification theorem.
fate: The concrete Gelfand--Ponomarev connection is \citet{gelfandponomarev1974modular}, published in 1974. The list of names alone does not warrant importing additional results.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is a historical attribution, not an independent open problem.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Every finite lattice embeds in a finite partition lattice
notes: A theorem attributed to Pudl\'ak and T\r{u}ma embeds every finite lattice in a lattice of equivalence relations; infimum is intersection and supremum is described using union.
statement: For every finite lattice \(L\), there exists a finite set \(X\) and an injective lattice homomorphism \(L\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Eq}(X)\). Meets in \(\operatorname{Eq}(X)\) are intersections; joins are the equivalence relations generated by unions, not the raw unions.
reconstruction: The lattice operations are made explicit. This embedding theorem is not the finite algebra congruence-lattice representation problem.
fate: The preliminary announcement is \citet{pudlaktuma1977every}. \citet[Conclusions]{pudlaktuma1980finite} gives a bounded embedding into \(\operatorname{Eq}(n)\) for sufficiently large \(n\); the full article appeared in December 1980 after receipt in 1977.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Elastic scattering and Mandelstam invariants
notes: For equal masses, \(p_1+q_1=p_2+q_2\), all four squares equal \(m^2\), and \(s=(p_1+q_1)^2\), \(t=(p_1-p_2)^2\), \(u=(p_1-q_2)^2\), with \(s+t+u=4m^2\). The notes also say total momentum is zero.
statement: For four on-shell Minkowski momenta with the stated conservation law, the displayed invariants obey \(s+t+u=4m^2\) by bilinear expansion. A zero total spatial momentum may specify the centre-of-mass frame; a zero sum of all incoming four-momenta requires reversing the outgoing momenta.
reconstruction: The frame convention is supplied to avoid interpreting positive-energy incoming four-momenta as having zero total energy. \ours\ Bilinear expansion, using \(p_2+q_2=p_1+q_1\) and the four mass-shell equations, verifies \(s+t+u=4m^2\).
fate: This is standard kinematic input to the pre-1985 dual-resonance construction, as in \citet{veneziano1968construction}. The invariant identity is verified directly from the notebook equations.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: The listed duality conditions
notes: The amplitude is analytic, symmetric in \(s,t\), has only simple \(s\)-poles at positions independent of \(t\), and has polynomial residues \(R_n(t)\) in \(\sum_{n\geq0}R_n(t)/(n-\alpha(s))\).
statement: The intended class consists of meromorphic crossing-symmetric functions whose pole divisors are \(\alpha(s)=n\) and \(\alpha(t)=n\), with polynomial residues in the crossed variable when \(\alpha\) is affine. A partial-fraction series additionally needs a convergence prescription or subtraction terms.
reconstruction: ``Analytic'' means holomorphic off the poles, not entire. Growth and normalization conditions are absent.
fate: The conditions belong to the historical dual-amplitude programme of \citet{veneziano1968construction}. Only publisher metadata was accessible for that original paper; the notebook conditions themselves are analyzed here without attributing a completeness theorem to it.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: The Veneziano beta amplitude and the unsupported uniqueness assertion
notes: The five conditions are said to determine uniquely \[A(s,t)=B(-\alpha(s),-\alpha(t))\].
statement: The beta function gives one meromorphic crossing-symmetric solution. For affine \(\alpha\), its residue at \(\alpha(s)=n\) is polynomial in \(\alpha(t)\). The listed properties alone do not fix even its overall nonzero scalar factor; unless a fully convergent pole expansion without an entire part is imposed, adding a crossing-symmetric polynomial also preserves the listed local pole properties.
reconstruction: \ours\ If \(A\) satisfies the listed homogeneous conditions, so does \(cA\) for every nonzero constant \(c\); this supplies the stated countercheck of uniqueness without normalization.
fate: The amplitude was published by \citet{veneziano1968construction} in September 1968, after receipt on 29 July. No uniqueness theorem under exactly the notebook hypotheses was verified; elementary counterexamples show why extra assumptions are necessary.
present_status: As of November 2026, the beta-function construction is classical; uniqueness under only the recorded conditions is false.

title: Linear Regge trajectories as physical input
notes: The linearity of \(\alpha(s)\) is attributed to analysis of experimental data.
statement: The model takes \(\alpha(s)=\alpha_0+\alpha's\), with intercept and slope supplied as parameters. This is a phenomenological assumption in the historical amplitude, not a mathematical consequence of the five conditions.
fate: The original title of \citet{veneziano1968construction} explicitly specifies linearly rising trajectories. The notebook supplies no experiment or numerical fit to audit.
present_status: As of November 2026, this item is a historical model assumption; no claim of exact linearity for all observed hadrons is inferred.

title: Euler integral for the four-point amplitude
notes: The beta amplitude is rewritten as a one-variable integral with exponents involving pairwise momentum products; the accompanying two-in/two-out diagram is followed by \(\sum_i p_i=0\).
statement: For \(\operatorname{Re}\alpha(s)<0\) and \(\operatorname{Re}\alpha(t)<0\), \[B(-\alpha(s),-\alpha(t))=\int_0^1 x^{-\alpha(s)-1}(1-x)^{-\alpha(t)-1}\,dx.\] Other values are defined by meromorphic continuation. Expressing the exponents through momenta additionally fixes the metric, mass shell, slope and all-incoming convention.
reconstruction: The unambiguous beta-integral formula replaces an identification of physical parameters that the notes do not fully normalize. Outgoing arrows alone do not implement all-incoming signed momenta.
fate: This is Euler's beta integral in the amplitude of \citet{veneziano1968construction}; no post-1985 mathematical development is needed.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Five-point Euler integrals and the meaning of closed evaluation
notes: A double integral with factors \(x,y,1-x,1-y,1-xy\) and omitted exponents is said not to have been calculated in general.
statement: For parameters \(a,b,c,d>0\) and real \(e<b+d\), the model integral \[\int_0^1\!\int_0^1x^{a-1}(1-x)^{b-1}y^{c-1}(1-y)^{d-1}(1-xy)^{-e}\,dx\,dy\] equals \[B(a,b)B(c,d)\,{}_3F_2\!\left(\begin{matrix}a,c,e\\a+b,c+d\end{matrix};1\right).\] This follows by the binomial expansion and beta integration, with continuation where justified. A special-function representation is different from a gamma-product evaluation.
reconstruction: The five-parameter integral and its evaluation are an editorial calculation, not a formula supplied by the notebook. No exact physical five-point amplitude or gamma-product conjecture is claimed. \ours\ Expanding \((1-xy)^{-e}\) and integrating each power gives the displayed beta factors and the \({}_3F_2\) series. \oursComputed\ The terminating specialization \(a=b=c=d=1,e=-2\) gives \(11/18\) independently by polynomial integration and by the hypergeometric expression; code and output are supplied. This checks an editorial model, not missing notebook exponents.
fate: The notebook omits the exponents and the intended class of answers. The displayed elementary reconstruction establishes that ``not calculated'' cannot be promoted to a precise general open problem. The four-point comparator is \citet{veneziano1968construction}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the notebook's intended evaluation question is not identifiable.

statement: Let \(g\) be a nondegenerate form on a \(d\)-dimensional space, indexed by \(0\leq\mu<d\). Use one oscillator of each positive integer frequency in each component, together with zero modes. The algebraic Fock space consists of finite products of negative-frequency generators acting on a momentum vacuum; infinitely many generators exist although each vector uses finitely many.
reconstruction: The index endpoint is corrected from \(d\) to \(d-1\). Finitely many species and countably many frequencies resolve the contradictory prose.
fate: The same Heisenberg representation is written in \citet[introduction, equations~(1)--(2)]{frenkel1985representations}, tracing the construction to the early dual-resonance literature.

title: Chiral coordinate fields and their distributional commutators
notes: The fields are \(P(\theta)=\sum_m a_me^{-im\theta}\) and \(Q(\theta)=x+p\theta+i\sum_{n\ne0}a_n e^{-in\theta}/n\). Their commutators involve \(\delta\), \(\delta'\), and a function called Heaviside.
statement:
With the corrected common index \(n\) in \(Q\), \(\partial_	heta Q=P\). In the distributional sense, \([Q^\mu(	heta),P^
u(	heta')]=2\pi i g^{\mu
u}\delta_{2\pi}(	heta-	heta')\) and \([P^\mu(	heta),P^

The local sign function, a lift of the angular coordinate, and distributional interpretation are supplied. \ours\ On \(0<|u|<2\pi\), the Fourier identity \(\sum_{n\ne0}e^{-inu}/n=-i(\pi\operatorname{sgn}u-u)\), together with the zero-mode commutator \(-iu\), yields the stated odd kernel. Differentiating the distributional series gives the two current commutators.
fate: These identities follow directly from the displayed oscillator brackets; the field formalism is the one used in \citet[introduction, equations~(1)--(4)]{frenkel1985representations}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Sugawara operators for free bosons
notes: \(L_m=(4\pi)^{-1}\int e^{im\theta}:P(\theta)^2:\,d\theta\), equivalently \(2L_m=\sum_{r+s=m}:a_ra_s:\), is asserted to satisfy Virasoro with central charge \(d\); this is an exercise. The formula for \(L_0\) is given.
statement: On algebraic Fock space, \[L_m=\tfrac12\sum_{r\in\mathbb Z}g_{\mu\nu}:a_r^\mu a_{m-r}^\nu:,\qquad L_0=\tfrac12(p,p)+\sum_{n>0}(a_{-n},a_n),\] and \[[L_m,L_n]=(m-n)L_{m+n}+\tfrac d{12}(m^3-m)\delta_{m,-n}I.\] Normal ordering puts annihilation operators on the right; each mode acts by a finite sum on a fixed finite-energy vector.
fate: The construction and the double-contraction calculation are given in \citet[section~2 and Theorem~3.3]{frenkel1985representations}. The signature of \(g\) does not change the central charge \(d\).
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Normal-ordered exponential vertex operators
notes: \(V(k,\theta)=\exp(i\langle k,Q(\theta)\rangle)\) is factorized at \(\theta=0\) into creation and annihilation exponentials with a momentum-shift factor \(e^{ikx}\).
statement: The exponential must be normal ordered. At \(z=1\), one may write \[Y_k(1)=\exp\!\left(\sum_{n>0}(k,a_{-n})/n\right)D_k\exp\!\left(-\sum_{n>0}(k,a_n)/n\right).\] The complete field is \(Y_k(z)=E_-(k,z)D_k z^{(k,a_0)}E_+(k,z)\), with an additional lattice cocycle when mutual locality is required.
reconstruction: Normal ordering and the zero-mode power for variable \(z\) are supplied; an unregularized exponential of the field has divergent self-contraction.
fate: Compare \citet[section~2.1, equation~(2.3)]{frenkel1985representations} and the original affine construction of \citet{frenkelkac1980basic} (published in 1980).
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Vertex covariance and conformal weight
notes: The notes give \(V(k,\theta)=e^{i\theta L_0}V(k)e^{-i\theta L_0}\) and \([L_n-L_0,V(k)]=n(k,k)V(k)/2\).
statement: For the plane primary field \(Y_k(z)\) of weight \(h=(k,k)/2\), \[[L_n,Y_k(z)]=\bigl(z^{n+1}\partial_z+(n+1)hz^n\bigr)Y_k(z).\] Evaluation at \(z=1\) gives the stated difference commutator. Angular translation and the cylinder field require a consistent choice of \(z=e^{\pm i\theta}\) and the factor \(z^h\).
reconstruction: The field of conformal weight \(h\), its plane/cylinder convention, and the zero-mode factor are essential. The note's two angular signs should not be combined without this convention choice.
fate: This is the standard free-boson covariance relation; \citet[section~2, vertex and Virasoro relations]{frenkel1985representations} provides the pre-1985 operator construction.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Factorizing amplitudes through vertices and a propagator
notes: The proposed vacuum expectation becomes a chain \[\langle0|V(p_2)D(s_2)V(p_3)\cdots D(s_{n-2})V(p_{n-1})|0\rangle\], with \(D(s)=\int_0^1x^{L_0-\alpha(s)-1}(1-x)^{\alpha(0)-1}\,dx\).
statement: On an eigenvector of the operator denoted by \(L_0\) with eigenvalue \(\lambda\), the displayed propagator is \(B(\lambda-\alpha(s),\alpha(0))\), initially for positive real parts of both arguments, and then meromorphically continued. In a full string amplitude one must specify whether this operator is the oscillator number operator or the full zero-mode-inclusive \(L_0\), the incoming/outgoing vacuum momenta, and vertex normalizations.
reconstruction: The spectral meaning of the integral is made explicit. The notebook reuses \(L_0\) in a way that may double-count the intermediate momentum if read literally. \ours\ The spectral formula follows by applying the displayed operator integral to an \(L_0\)-eigenvector and then recognizing Euler's beta integral.
fate: The method belongs to the established dual-resonance operator formalism discussed by \citet[introduction]{frenkel1985representations}. No exact equality of the notebook's incompletely normalized chain with every physical amplitude is asserted.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Momentum Fock spaces and mode shifts
notes: Vacua satisfy \(a_n|0,p\rangle=0\) for \(n>0\) and \(a_0|0,p\rangle=p|0,p\rangle\). Vertex modes map \(H(p)\to H(p+k)\) and satisfy \([a_m^\mu,V_n(k)]=k_\mu V_{n+m}(k)\).
statement: Let \(H(p)=S(\bigoplus_{n>0}\mathbb C^d t^{-n})|p\rangle\). Then \([a_0^\mu,Y_k(z)]=k^\mu Y_k(z)\) and \([a_m^\mu,Y_k(z)]=k^\mu z^mY_k(z)\). With the convention \(Y_k(z)=\sum_nY_{k,n}z^{-n}\), the mode relation is \([a_m^\mu,Y_{k,n}]=k^\mu Y_{k,n+m}\). Integral mode labels require the appropriate integral momentum pairings; otherwise shifted powers occur.
reconstruction: An algebraic sum over chosen momenta is sufficient for formal fields; a Hilbert-space direct integral over continuous momenta is a different completion.
fate: \citet[section~2.1, equations~(2.2)--(2.4)]{frenkel1985representations} gives this construction. The upper/lower target index must be raised or lowered consistently with \(g\).
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: The two-vertex contraction and binomial generating series
notes: An exercise asserts \(\sum_n A_nz^n=(1-z)^{(k_1,k_2)}\) for two vertex modes. The final momentum in the bra is written \(p+k_1+k\), without the second subscript.
statement: For the oscillator parts of two normal-ordered vertices, in the radial region \(|z|<1\), contraction gives \[\exp\!\left(-(k_1,k_2)\sum_{n>0}\frac{z^n}{n}\right)=(1-z)^{(k_1,k_2)}.\] Thus the normalized oscillator coefficients are \(A_n=(-1)^n\binom{(k_1,k_2)}n\). The full matrix element also contains the zero-mode monomial and has final momentum \(p+k_1+k_2\).
reconstruction: ``Normalized oscillator coefficients'' separates the stated contraction from omitted zero-mode powers and the possible shift of Laurent indices. \ours\ The oscillator commutator of the two exponential exponents is the scalar \(-(k_1,k_2)\sum_{n>0}z^n/n\); exponentiation and \(-\log(1-z)=\sum_{n>0}z^n/n\) give the generating series.
fate: The calculation is the two-field instance of the vertex product formula in \citet[equation~(2.5)]{frenkel1985representations}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Virasoro weights and the physical constraint space
notes: The continuation introduces weight vectors, highest weight, and \(\widetilde{\mathcal H}=\{v:L_0v=v,\ L_iv=0\ (i>0)\}\).
statement: For a Virasoro module with diagonalizable \(L_0\), the relation \([L_0,L_n]=-nL_n\) makes \(L_n\) lower the \(L_0\)-eigenvalue by \(n\). The physical constraint space at intercept one is \(P^1=\ker(L_0-1)\cap\bigcap_{n>0}\ker L_n\). It is a subspace of highest-weight vectors, not a Virasoro submodule in general.
fate: This is the standard constraint space in \citet[equations~(8) and (4.1)]{frenkel1985representations}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Spurious states and the physical quotient
notes: The set of spurions is written as those physical \(v\) expressible as one \(L_iv'\), \(i<0\), and the physical space is its quotient.
statement: In an algebraic free-boson Fock module with its invariant Hermitian form, put \(S=\sum_{n>0}L_{-n}H\) and \(N=P^1\cap S\). The linear quotient \(P^1/N\) is well defined. In each finite-dimensional energy space, adjointness \(L_n^*=L_{-n}\) identifies \(N\) with the radical of the restricted form on \(P^1\). A union of individual images need not be a subspace.
reconstruction: The sum of images and the invariant form are supplied. The equivalence with the radical uses finite-dimensionality of each fixed-momentum energy level and its nondegenerate ambient form. \ours\ At a fixed finite-dimensional energy level, adjointness gives \(P^1=S^\perp\); nondegeneracy of the ambient form gives \((P^1)^\perp=S\). Thus its radical is \(P^1\cap S\), verifying the corrected quotient algebraically.
fate: The transverse/spurious decomposition occurs in \citet[section~4, Lemmas~4.2--4.3]{frenkel1985representations}; \citet[section~5, Theorem~5.1]{borcherds1992monstrous} explicitly uses the quotient by the null space in a later application.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: The weight of a preimage under L minus one
notes: Equation (5) says that if \(L_{-1}v'=v\) has weight one then \(v'\) has weight two.
statement: If \(v'\) is a weight vector, \(L_{-1}v'\ne0\), and \(L_0L_{-1}v'=L_{-1}v'\), then \(L_0v'=0\). Indeed, \([L_0,L_{-1}]=L_{-1}\), so \(L_{-1}\) raises the weight by one.
reconstruction: \ours\ For a weight-\(h\) vector, the bracket gives \(L_0L_{-1}v'=(h+1)L_{-1}v'\). A nonzero weight-one image forces \(h=0\).
fate: The correction is forced by the Virasoro bracket, for example \citet[equation~(2.9)]{frenkel1985representations}. The scan clearly contains both the word ``two'' and \(2v'\); this is a faithful mathematical error, not a translation correction.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Half constraints followed by a quotient
notes: Genuine invariants under diffeomorphisms are obstructed by the nontrivial centre. The proposed procedure takes invariants for one half and quotients by the action of the other half.
statement: The construction \(P^1/(P^1\cap\sum_{n>0}L_{-n}H)\) imposes the positive-mode constraints and removes the spurious descendants. It is not the subspace annihilated by every Virasoro operator: with nonzero central charge, such an ordinary invariant subspace is zero.
reconstruction: The quotation marks around ``invariants'' are retained in substance; no unstated equivalence with an arbitrary cohomology theory is attributed to the speaker.
fate: The physical quotient is the established pre-1985 construction summarized in \citet[section~4]{frenkel1985representations}. A full cohomological or BRST reformulation is not specified in this notebook passage.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: The critical no-ghost theorem
notes: The two goals are a description by \(d-2\) oscillators and strict positivity on the physical quotient; both are said to hold for \(d=26\). The parenthesis calls this absence of tachyons.
statement: For the bosonic Fock space with one negative and twenty-five positive directions, intercept one, and nonzero real momentum \(p\), the form on \(P^1(p)\) is positive semidefinite. Its quotient by the radical is positive definite and has the transverse oscillator multiplicities of twenty-four bosons at level \(N=1-(p,p)/2\), when \(N\) is a nonnegative integer. Strict positivity applies to nonzero quotient vectors. Zero momentum must be excluded: its level-one physical space contains the full indefinite target space.
reconstruction: The momentum hypothesis, quotient by null vectors and level condition are supplied. Positivity removes negative-norm ghosts; it does not remove the bosonic ground-state tachyon. \ours\ The zero-momentum exception can be checked directly: every level-one vector \(a_{-1}(v)|0\rangle\) obeys all positive-mode constraints and inherits the target-space form, which is indefinite. This is a check of a known exception, not a proof of no-ghost.
fate: No-ghost was established in the early 1970s. The exact zero-momentum exception and the critical transverse proof can be checked in \citet[Theorem~4.1 and Lemmas~4.2--4.3]{frenkel1985representations}; a later general form is \citet[Theorem~5.1]{borcherds1992monstrous}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the theorem is classical. The notebook assertion becomes correct with these hypotheses; its identification with absence of tachyons is false.

title: The creation coefficient and zero modes in the continued vertex formula
notes: Equation (6) writes the creation exponential without \(1/n\), followed by \(D_p\) and the correctly divided annihilation exponential. Equation (7) defines the momentum shift.
statement: The oscillator factors must both have frequency denominators: \(E_-(p,z)=\exp(\sum_{n>0}(p,a_{-n})z^n/n)\) and \(E_+(p,z)=\exp(-\sum_{n>0}(p,a_n)z^{-n}/n)\). The plane field is \(Y_p(z)=E_-(p,z)D_pz^{(p,a_0)}E_+(p,z)\). Its cylinder-normalized counterpart is \(X_p(z)=z^{(p,p)/2}Y_p(z)\), up to consistently ordered zero-mode factors.
reconstruction: The scan confirms the missing creation denominator. Plane and cylinder fields are distinguished so that the subsequent \(dz/z\) residue is meaningful. \ours\ In a single mode, represent \(a_{-n}\) by multiplication by \(u\) and \(a_n\) by \(n\partial_u\). The creation exponential then has the required commutator precisely with coefficient \(1/n\). \oursComputed\ This differential-operator identity was checked for frequencies one through six on \(u^3+u+1\); omitting the denominator multiplies the result by \(n\).
fate: Compare \citet[equations~(2.2)--(2.3)]{frenkel1985representations}. In that source the exponential of the sum of zero-mode operators incorporates a scalar power through their commutator; replacing it by a bare translation loses this factor.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Multipoint oscillator contractions
notes: Equation (8) gives a vacuum matrix element as \(\prod_{j>1}(1-z_j/z_i)^{(p_i,p_j)}\).
statement: For corrected, oscillator-stripped vertices in the radial region \(|z_1|>\cdots>|z_r|\), their normalized contraction is \[\prod_{1\leq i<j\leq r}(1-z_j/z_i)^{(p_i,p_j)}.\] A full matrix element of \(Y_{p_i}\), between initial momentum \(k\) and final momentum \(k+\sum_i p_i\), also contains the zero-mode monomial \(\prod_i z_i^{(p_i,k+\sum_{j>i}p_j)}\), as well as any chosen cocycle factors.
reconstruction: The product index is changed from \(j>1\) to \(i<j\); the extra powers assume the displayed order of plane-field zero modes. The oscillator identity is not the full correlation function without this qualification. \ours\ Acting from right to left, the momentum immediately before \(Y_{p_i}\) is \(k+\sum_{j>i}p_j\), which gives the displayed zero-mode monomial. This verifies that the stripped contraction and full matrix element differ.
fate: The repeated two-field contraction follows from \citet[equation~(2.5)]{frenkel1985representations}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Norm-two screening operators commute with Virasoro
notes: The integrals \(\int X(p,z)\,dz/z\) are to commute with Virasoro when \((p,p)=2\).
statement: If \(Y_p(z)\) is a primary field of weight one with integral Laurent powers on the chosen momentum sectors, then \(Q_p=\operatorname{Res}_{z=0}Y_p(z)\,dz\) commutes with every \(L_n\), because its commutator is the residue of \(\partial_z(z^{n+1}Y_p)\). For \(X_p=zY_p\), this is equivalently \(\operatorname{Res}X_p(z)\,dz/z\). Free-boson weight one means \((p,p)=2\).
reconstruction: The notebook operator lacks the necessary zero-mode normalization; its formula cannot be used literally in this residue assertion. Residue notation replaces an unspecified contour and factor \(2\pi i\). \ours\ The residue of the derivative of any integral Laurent series is zero, proving the displayed commutation assertion from the primary-field transformation law.
fate: The commuting zero modes are part of \citet[equations~(2.10)--(2.12)]{frenkel1985representations}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: A symmetric Cartan matrix from Lorentzian vectors
notes: Vectors \(p_i\in\mathbb R^{26}\) have square two and integral products \(A_{ij}\), followed by the unrestricted inequality \(A_{ij}<0\).
statement: The intended symmetric generalized Cartan conditions are \(A_{ii}=2\), \(A_{ij}\in\mathbb Z_{\leq0}\) for \(i\ne j\), and \(A_{ij}=0\iff A_{ji}=0\). A realization as a Gram matrix in signature \((25,1)\) is an additional restriction: its positive and negative inertia indices are at most twenty-five and one, respectively, and its rank is at most twenty-six.
reconstruction: The negative sign applies off the diagonal and allows zero. The inertia restrictions are elementary consequences of a Gram realization. \ours\ The Gram matrix is the pullback of the ambient form under the column map \(\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{26}\); a positive or negative definite subspace maps injectively into one of the corresponding sign in the target. This proves the stated necessary inertia bounds.
fate: The exact Cartan conditions appear in \citet[section~1.1]{frenkel1985representations}. No assertion that every symmetric Cartan matrix fits this fixed Lorentzian space is warranted.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Kac--Moody Chevalley operators from screening residues
notes: The norm-two vertex residues \(e_i,f_i\), together with \(h_i|k\rangle=(k,p_i)|k\rangle\), are asserted to represent the algebra with Cartan matrix \(A\). Macdonald at Bourbaki is recommended.
statement: For a symmetric nonaffine Kac--Moody algebra and its standard lattice/Heisenberg vertex construction, a compatible bimultiplicative sign cocycle gives screening operators for the simple roots and their negatives satisfying the Chevalley--Serre relations. The sign of \(f_i\) is chosen to match either \([e_i,f_i]=h_i\) or the opposite Chevalley convention. In the affine case one uses the separate basic current-algebra construction, rather than assuming the same nondegenerate root-space model.
reconstruction: The cocycle, zero modes and representation-space hypotheses are indispensable additions. The notebook outline is not an unrestricted construction from any list of Lorentzian vectors.
fate: \citet[Theorem~2.1]{frenkel1985representations} proves the nonaffine statement and explicitly separates its affine Theorem~2.2. The suggested reading is identifiable as \citet{macdonald1981affine}, Bourbaki expos\'e~577, June 1981.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Gelfand on the Monster, strings, and moonshine
notes: Gelfand connects the group of approximately \(10^{54}\) elements with strings, says ``the largest finite simple group'', and recalls work of Frenkel, Lepowsky and an unnamed third author.
statement: The intended group is the Monster, the largest sporadic finite simple group; finite simple groups as a whole have unbounded orders. The third author is Arne Meurman. The mathematical connection is the construction of a graded Monster representation with normalized modular \(J\)-character, and the later proof of the moonshine conjectures by vertex-algebra and no-ghost methods.
fate: Frenkel--Lepowsky--Meurman announced their module in May 1984 \citep{frenkellepowskymeurman1984natural}, before this intervention. \citet[Theorem~1.1 and sections~5--6]{borcherds1992monstrous} subsequently proved the moonshine assertions. That later theorem is a development of the connection, not proof of a precise conjecture stated here.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an identifiable pre-1985 mathematical connection with major later development. The notebook records no exact moonshine conjecture to classify separately.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Null directions and transverse DDF operators
notes: For a null vector \(p\), the vectors \(v^1,\ldots,v^{d-2},p\) form a basis of \(p^\perp\). The residues \(U_n(v)=\int v(z)X(np,z)\,dz/z\) are asserted to be oscillators.
statement: Let \(c\ne0\) be null in a real space of signature \((d-1,1)\). The quotient \(c^\perp/\mathbb Rc\) is positive definite of dimension \(d-2\). Choose orthonormal transverse representatives. Correctly normal-ordered DDF residues then satisfy \([A_m^i,A_n^j]=m\delta_{ij}\delta_{m,-n}(c,a_0)\); on a momentum tower with \((c,a_0)=1\), this is the standard Heisenberg relation. Sign changes in the exponential and mode labels must be made together.
reconstruction: Nonzero \(c\), orthonormality in the quotient and normalization of its pairing with the momentum are absent from the notes and supplied here. Mere linear independence gives the Gram matrix in the commutator, not \(\delta_{ij}\).
fate: \citet[introduction, equations~(4)--(5), and section~4]{frenkel1985representations} gives the residues and their central factor. The original Del Giudice--Di Vecchia--Fubini construction dates to 1972, as identified in that bibliography.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Completeness of transverse oscillators at the critical dimension
notes: After the Heisenberg assertion, the notes say that the operators generate the whole space.
statement: At \(d=26\), fixed nonzero physical momentum and level, DDF transverse states provide representatives for every class in the physical quotient by null/spurious states. A chosen DDF vacuum generates its compatible momentum tower, not every momentum sector from one vector. At zero momentum the usual positive-definite completeness statement has an exceptional sector.
reconstruction: The words ``whole space'' are restricted to the physical quotient and the momentum sectors on which the chosen DDF operators act.
fate: \citet[section~4, Lemmas~4.2--4.3 and equations~(4.8)--(4.9)]{frenkel1985representations} supplies the critical-dimension transverse description.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Borel presentation of the cohomology of the full flag variety
notes: For complete flags in \(V^n\), the first description is \(H^*(X,\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/J\), where \(J\) is generated by symmetric polynomials with no constant term.
statement: For \(X=\operatorname{Fl}(\mathbb C^n)\), let \(x_i\) be consistently signed first Chern classes of the tautological line quotients. Then \(H^*(X;\mathbb Q)\cong\mathbb Q[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(e_1,\ldots,e_n)\), with \(\deg x_i=2\). The ideal equals that generated by all positive-degree symmetric polynomials.
reconstruction: The field \(\mathbb C\), cohomological grading and signs of Chern generators are specified.
fate: The Borel presentation is recalled by \citet[section~1]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1973schubert}. The notebook explicitly presents the lecture as exposition of BGG and Lascoux--Sch\"utzenberger.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Bruhat cells and the homology/cohomology bases
notes: The orbit of the permuted standard flag under transformations preserving the standard flag is \(C_w\), with complex dimension \(\ell(w)\). Cells are said to form the homology basis; dual classes have degree \(2\ell(w)\).
statement: The Borel orbits \(C_w=BwB/B\) are affine spaces \(\mathbb C^{\ell(w)}\). Their closures \(\overline{C_w}\) have fundamental classes forming a basis of ordinary homology. The Kronecker-dual cohomology basis has degrees \(2\ell(w)\). With the standard opposite-Schubert convention, these are the Schubert classes represented by the polynomials below.
reconstruction: The duality here is evaluation on homology classes, not an unqualified identification of a cell with its Poincar\'e-dual class of complementary degree.
fate: \citet[section~2, in particular Theorem~2.11]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1973schubert} treats the cells and their closures. The passage from cells to fundamental classes of closures is essential.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Schubert polynomial representatives
notes: BGG classes modulo \(J\) have been lifted to actual polynomials of degree \(\ell(w)\), with \(P_{\mathrm{id}}=1\) and \(P_{w_0}=x_1^{n-1}x_2^{n-2}\cdots x_{n-1}\).
statement: The Lascoux--Sch\"utzenberger Schubert polynomial \(\mathfrak S_w\in\mathbb Z[x_1,x_2,\ldots]\) is homogeneous of ordinary polynomial degree \(\ell(w)\); for \(w\in S_n\), the longest-element polynomial is \(x^\delta=x_1^{n-1}x_2^{n-2}\cdots x_{n-1}\). Its class in the Borel quotient represents the corresponding Schubert class.
reconstruction: The canonical choice involves stability and divided differences, not merely an arbitrary lifting of a residue class.
fate: \citet[Definition~1.3]{lascouxschutzenberger1982schubert} defines these polynomials; the note appeared on 29 March 1982. Their 1983 longer account also predates this seminar \citep{lascouxschutzenberger1983symmetry}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Normalization of the top cohomology class
notes: The Vandermonde \(\prod_{i<j}(x_i-x_j)\) is called the same class modulo \(J\) as \(x^\delta\). An alternative is \(\rho^{m(n-1)/2}/(m(n-1)/2)!\).
statement: Write \(N=n(n-1)/2\) and \(\rho=(n-1)x_1+(n-2)x_2+\cdots+x_{n-1}\). With compatible positive-root conventions, \[x^\delta\equiv\frac1{n!}\prod_{i<j}(x_i-x_j)\equiv\frac{\rho^N}{N!}\pmod J.\] The unnormalized Vandermonde represents \(n!\) times the top generator. Already for \(n=2\), \(x_1-x_2\equiv2x_1\).
reconstruction: \ours\ The \(n=2\) identity \(x_2\equiv-x_1\pmod J\) already detects the missing factor. \oursComputed\ Exact Gr\"obner reductions for \(n=2,3,4\) separately checked the Vandermonde and \(\rho\)-power normalizations. The general identities are the cited BGG results.
fate: \citet[Theorem~3.15 and Corollary~3.16]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1973schubert} gives the normalization and the \(\rho\)-power formula. The scan confirms both the absent \(1/n!\) and the letter \(m\) in the exponent.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: The sign convention for divided differences
notes: The numerator is \(f-s_if\), but the denominator is written \(x_{i+1}-x_i\).
statement: The convention compatible with \(\mathfrak S_{w_0}=x^\delta\), \(\mathfrak S_{\mathrm{id}}=1\), and the usual positive Schubert polynomials is \[\partial_i f=\frac{f-s_if}{x_i-x_{i+1}}.\] This is again a polynomial. The opposite denominator changes the sign of each operator and hence contributes \((-1)^{\ell(w)}\) to a reduced product.
reconstruction: Opposite-sign divided differences are mathematically legitimate if every accompanying formula is adjusted. The recorded top and identity classes make the unadjusted collection inconsistent. \ours\ The countercheck \(\partial_1x_1=1\) determines the compatible denominator sign. \oursComputed\ Exact polynomial calculations also checked square-zero and the braid identity on a nontrivial input and the longest-word top-to-one recurrence for \(n=2,3,4\). These finite audits do not replace the cited general theorem.
fate: Compare \citet[equations~(1.1)--(1.2)]{lascouxschutzenberger1982schubert} and \citet[Lemma~3.3]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1973schubert}. The smallest check is \(\partial_1x_1=1\); the notebook convention gives \(-1\).
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Independence of reduced expressions
notes: An operator \(A_w\) is obtained from a reduced product of adjacent transpositions and asserted independent of the decomposition. The last displayed transposition has a misplaced subscript.
statement: The operators \(\partial_i\) satisfy \(\partial_i^2=0\), \(\partial_i\partial_j=\partial_j\partial_i\) for \(|i-j|>1\), and \(\partial_i\partial_{i+1}\partial_i=\partial_{i+1}\partial_i\partial_{i+1}\). Thus \(\partial_w\) is independent of a reduced expression \(w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_{\ell(w)}}\). A nonreduced product of this length pattern vanishes when the corresponding word is not reduced.
reconstruction: The factors are adjacent simple reflections, not arbitrary inversions. The last factor is \((i_{\ell(w)},i_{\ell(w)}+1)\).
fate: The exact reduced/nonreduced statement is \citet[Theorem~3.4]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1973schubert}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Generating all Schubert polynomials from the longest element
notes: The displayed formula is \(P_w=A_{w_0w^{-1}}P_{w_0}\).
statement: Under the usual left composition convention \(\partial_u=\partial_{i_1}\cdots\partial_{i_r}\) for \(u=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_r}\), one has \[\mathfrak S_w=\partial_{w^{-1}w_0}x^\delta.\] Equivalently, apply \(\partial_i\) whenever replacing the current permutation \(v\) by \(vs_i\) lowers its length. An opposite action convention reverses the product indexing.
reconstruction: The notebook does not specify left versus right operator action. Its \(w_0w^{-1}\) is therefore treated as a convention ambiguity rather than an isolated transcription error.
fate: \citet[Definition~1.3]{lascouxschutzenberger1982schubert} gives the construction; \citet[section~3]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1973schubert} provides its cohomological precursor.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Symmetry at a non-descent
notes: \(P_w\) is symmetric in \(x_i,x_{i+1}\) if \((i,i+1)\) is not an inversion of \(w\).
statement: For the usual Schubert polynomial, \(s_i\mathfrak S_w=\mathfrak S_w\) if and only if \(w(i)<w(i+1)\), equivalently \(\ell(ws_i)>\ell(w)\). Indeed \(\partial_i\mathfrak S_w=0\) in this case, whereas for a right descent it equals the nonzero polynomial \(\mathfrak S_{ws_i}\).
reconstruction: The notebook records the valid sufficient direction. ``Inversion'' is made precise as an adjacent right descent, not a value-based left descent.
fate: The exact equivalence is stated immediately after \citet[Definition~1.3]{lascouxschutzenberger1982schubert}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

notes: The lecture restarts with \(L_i=:\sum_{m+n=i}g_{\mu\nu}a_m^\mu a_n^\nu:\), followed by the standard Virasoro bracket. Normal ordering is said to make the expression meaningful and only add a constant.

Moving annihilation modes to the right makes each mode locally finite on algebraic Fock vectors. Reordering a finite truncation changes it by a scalar, but the infinite unrenormalized scalar need not converge; it is not an ordinary finite constant that may simply be added.
