title: Gelfand asks for normal ordering on other underlying spaces
notes: Gelfand asks what is needed for the operation \(:\ :\), and what happens for a lattice, torus or sphere.
statement: The question asks which choices of geometry, modes, polarization and vacuum permit normal ordering and an analogue of the resulting centrally extended algebra. It does not say whether ``torus'' and ``sphere'' are world sheets, spatial manifolds or target spaces, nor which algebra should replace Virasoro.

title: Gelfand identifies the classical vector fields and their central extension
notes: Gelfand writes \(L_n=e^{int}d/dt\) in the classical theory and compares its one-dimensional quantum extension with \([d/dx,x]=1\).
statement: The complex vector fields \(D_n=i e^{int}d/dt\) satisfy \([D_m,D_n]=(m-n)D_{m+n}\). Their standard nontrivial one-dimensional central extension has cocycle \((m^3-m)\delta_{m,-n}/12\), giving Virasoro. The displayed unscaled fields satisfy the same relation with an extra factor of \(i\). The Heisenberg comparison is structural, not an identification of the two cocycles.

title: When the Virasoro Fock module depends only on momentum norm
notes: The notes assert \(\mathcal H_p\cong\mathcal H_{p'}\) whenever \((p,p)=(p',p')\), and label the module only by this scalar.
statement: An isometry of the target form carrying \(p\) to \(p'\) induces a Virasoro-module isomorphism. In a real Lorentzian space, equal nonzero norms give such an isometry, as do two nonzero null vectors. Zero and a nonzero null vector are an exception despite equal norm: on level one, \(L_1(a_{-1}(v)|p\rangle)=(v,p)|p\rangle\), a rank-zero map for \(p=0\) and rank-one map for \(p\ne0\). Hence these graded Virasoro modules are not isomorphic.
reconstruction: The isometry-orbit argument gives a sufficient statement. The level-one calculation isolates a literal counterexample in the Lorentzian setting actually used by these lectures. \ours\ The level-one rank calculation supplies a literal counterexample to the norm-only assertion. \oursComputed\ A two-dimensional Lorentzian block with momenta \(0\) and \((1,1)\) has equal norm zero but the two ranks are zero and one; the block embeds in the twenty-six-dimensional target.
fate: The countercheck is immediate from the standard relations in \citet[equations~(2.2), (2.10), (2.14)]{frenkel1985representations}. It is a correction of an expository claim, not a new unresolved representation problem.
present_status: As of November 2026, the norm-only assertion is false without excluding the zero/nonzero-null distinction.

title: Summing momentum sectors before imposing the constraints
notes: The module \(\bigoplus_{(p,p)\in\mathbb R}\mathcal H_{(p,p)}\) is used to construct physical states, with the comment that the construction depends only on the Virasoro action.
statement: One may form an algebraic direct sum of chosen Virasoro modules and impose \(P^1\) and its spurious quotient componentwise. For the subsequent vertex action, however, the summands must retain actual momenta in a set closed under the required shifts; one representative for each numerical norm does not specify those maps. Positivity also uses the invariant form, not the abstract Virasoro action alone.
reconstruction: The statement separates a legitimate abstract module sum from the extra momentum and form data required later.
fate: The momentum-labelled lattice sum \(S(\mathfrak h^-)\otimes\mathbb C[\Gamma]\) is explicit in \citet[section~2.1, equation~(2.2)]{frenkel1985representations}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: The repeated no-ghost statement uses the quotient, not all constrained states
notes: The theorem says that twenty-four commuting oscillators generate \(\widetilde{\mathcal H}\) from a vacuum, and that its inherited form is positive definite, only when \(d=26\).
statement: In the critical Lorentzian bosonic theory at nonzero momentum, constrained physical states have a positive semidefinite form; the quotient by its radical is positive definite and is represented by transverse DDF states. Spurious null vectors remain before quotienting. A single chosen DDF vacuum generates a normalized momentum tower, not the unrestricted direct sum of all momenta.
reconstruction: The inserted tilde in the manuscript is preserved in notes but corrected in the mathematical statement. Zero momentum is again excluded.
fate: The exact qualifications are given in \citet[Theorem~4.1 and section~4]{frenkel1985representations}; compare \citet[Theorem~5.1]{borcherds1992monstrous}. The positive-semidefinite assertion also has subcritical variants, so ``only 26'' should refer to the precise twenty-four-oscillator critical completeness statement.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: The corrected oscillator vertex formula still omits zero-mode powers
notes: Equation (9) now includes \(1/n\) in both exponentials and defines \(D_p|k\rangle=|k+p\rangle\).
statement: This is a valid oscillator-stripped momentum-shifting series. To obtain the plane primary field one must also include \(z^{(p,a_0)}\); the cylinder-normalized field includes \(z^{(p,p)/2}\) as well. Integral pairings are needed for unshifted integral Laurent modes on a lattice sum.
fate: The complete expression and mode convention are \citet[equation~(2.3)]{frenkel1985representations}. This passage repairs the denominator missing on P001237, but does not itself restore the zero modes.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: The Laurent-mode sign in the Heisenberg commutator
notes: The expansion is \(X(p,z)=\sum_iX_i(p)z^i\), while equation (12) asserts \([a_n^\mu,X_i(p)]=p^\mu X_{i+n}(p)\).
statement: The field relation is \([a_n^\mu,X(p,z)]=p^\mu z^nX(p,z)\). With \(X=\sum_iX_i z^i\), coefficient comparison gives \([a_n^\mu,X_i]=p^\mu X_{i-n}\). The recorded plus sign is correct only for the alternative expansion \(X=\sum_iX_i z^{-i}\).
reconstruction: \ours\ The coefficient of \(z^i\) in \(z^n\sum_jX_jz^j\) is \(X_{i-n}\). \oursComputed\ Twenty-five exact Laurent-coefficient comparisons confirm this indexing; the general correction is the coefficient identity itself.
fate: The negative-exponent convention occurs in \citet[equations~(2.3)--(2.4)]{frenkel1985representations}. Both conflicting signs in the notebook are clear in the scan.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Integral, even, and unimodular lattices
notes: The lattice \(Q\subset\mathbb R^d\) is integral and unimodular when its Gram entries are integers and their determinant is one. Evenness is \((\gamma,\gamma)\in2\mathbb Z\).
statement: A full-rank lattice in a nondegenerate real quadratic space is integral if \((Q,Q)\subset\mathbb Z\), even if every norm is even, and unimodular if \(Q=Q^*\), equivalently the Gram determinant has absolute value one. In the positive-definite case used for the finite root system below, this determinant is \(+1\).
reconstruction: The rank and signature assumptions are stated. Indefinite unimodular Gram determinants can be \(-1\).
fate: These standard definitions are recalled in \citet[section~1]{brouwerleech}. They precede the seminar; the reference is an undated modern exposition, not a priority claim.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Norm-two roots of an integral positive-definite lattice
notes: A root is a lattice vector of squared length two; later \(\Delta\) denotes the set of all such vectors and positivity is imposed.
statement: For a positive-definite integral lattice \(Q\), \(\Delta=\{\alpha\in Q:(\alpha,\alpha)=2\}\) is finite. The reflections \(s_\alpha(v)=v-(v,\alpha)\alpha\) preserve \(Q\) and \(\Delta\). Thus \(\Delta\) is a reduced simply laced crystallographic root system in its span, possibly empty or reducible; its components have types \(A,D,E\).
reconstruction: Positivity is essential to finiteness. Roots need not span the entire lattice space.
fate: The finite simply laced root-system construction is the setting of \citet[section~1.1, equation~(1.3)]{frenkel1985representations}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: The rank restriction for even unimodular positive lattices
notes: Immediately after defining roots, the notes say ``such'' objects exist only in dimensions divisible by eight.
statement: A positive-definite even unimodular lattice has rank divisible by eight. Conversely, for every positive multiple \(8r\), the orthogonal sum \(E_8^{\oplus r}\) provides one. This statement concerns lattices with all three hypotheses, not norm-two roots; for example the rank-one root lattice \(A_1\) already has roots.
reconstruction: The antecedent of ``such'' is resolved using the preceding integral/even/unimodular assumptions. In indefinite signature the appropriate restriction is on the signature difference.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1.2]{brouwerleech} states the divisibility result and its theta-series context. This is a classical theorem, not a post-1985 development.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: The eight-dimensional lattice exercise
notes: The exercise is to construct such a lattice in \(\mathbb R^8\).
statement: Let \(D_8=\{x\in\mathbb Z^8:\sum_i x_i\equiv0\pmod2\}\) and \(h=(1/2,\ldots,1/2)\). Then \(E_8=D_8\cup(D_8+h)\) is a lattice: \(2h\in D_8\). It is integral and even since \((h,h)=2\) and \((x,h)=\frac12\sum x_i\in\mathbb Z\) on \(D_8\). Its covolume is \(\operatorname{covol}(D_8)/2=1\), hence it is unimodular.
reconstruction: The coordinates and the elementary verification are supplied by the companion. \ours\ The parity, integrality and index-two covolume verification constitute the supplied proof of the standard \(E_8\) exercise.
fate: This explicit standard construction solves the notebook exercise; \citet[section~1]{brouwerleech} supplies the surrounding even-unimodular lattice context. No novelty is claimed for the construction.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: ADE root lattices are even
notes: An aside says that root lattices of the \(A,D,E\) series satisfy condition (14), namely evenness.
statement: With every root normalized to squared length two, an integral linear combination of simple roots has even norm, because diagonal terms are even and cross terms occur twice. Thus simply laced root lattices are even. They need not be unimodular; evenness, not condition (13), is the recorded assertion.
reconstruction: \ours\ For \(v=\sum n_i\alpha_i\), the norm is \(2\sum_i n_i^2+2\sum_{i<j}n_in_j(\alpha_i,\alpha_j)\), an even integer.
fate: The normalization and root-lattice setting are in \citet[section~1.1]{frenkel1985representations}. The elementary expansion proves the exact notebook assertion.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: The sign cocycle forces evenness
notes: The lattice is now said not necessarily to be even, yet \(\varepsilon(\alpha,\beta)\varepsilon(\beta,\alpha)=(-1)^{(\alpha,\beta)}\) is required for every pair, with \(\varepsilon(\alpha,\alpha)=-1\) on roots.
statement: For an even integral free abelian lattice, choose a bimultiplicative normalized cocycle \(\varepsilon:Q\times Q\to\{\pm1\}\) with commutator \((-1)^{(\alpha,\beta)}\) and diagonal \(\varepsilon(\alpha,\alpha)=(-1)^{(\alpha,\alpha)/2}\). Such a choice is made on an ordered lattice basis and extended multiplicatively. The displayed commutator identity itself forces evenness on setting \(\alpha=\beta\), since the left side equals one. An arbitrary function with the two displayed identities need not satisfy the cocycle identity.
reconstruction: Evenness and bimultiplicativity are restored. Odd-lattice superalgebra conventions require a different commutator sign and are not silently substituted. \ours\ Substitution \(\beta=\alpha\) gives \(1=(-1)^{(\alpha,\alpha)}\), directly contradicting the allowance of odd norms.
fate: The word ``bilinear'' and the existence argument on a basis are explicit in \citet[equation~(1.2) and following paragraph]{frenkel1985representations}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: A finite Lie algebra from the lattice roots
notes: The space \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak h\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Delta}\mathbb Cx_\alpha\) is given root brackets using \(\varepsilon\), including \([x_\alpha,x_{-\alpha}]=-\alpha\), and called an important construction of simple algebras.
statement: For a positive-definite even integral lattice and the cocycle just specified, set \([h,h']=0\), \([h,x_\alpha]=(h,\alpha)x_\alpha\), use \(\varepsilon(\alpha,\beta)x_{\alpha+\beta}\) when \(\alpha+\beta\in\Delta\), zero when the sum is neither a root nor zero, and \([x_\alpha,x_{-\alpha}]=-\alpha\). This gives a reductive complex Lie algebra. It is semisimple when roots span \(\mathfrak h\), and simple when they also form an irreducible root system. The orthogonal complement of their span is central.
reconstruction: The Cartan bracket and the spanning/irreducibility hypotheses are supplied. For a rootless lattice the displayed algebra is abelian, not simple. \ours\ If \(\Delta=\varnothing\), the displayed vector space is just the abelian Cartan space, which checks why simplicity cannot be claimed under the notebook assumptions alone.
fate: \citet[equation~(1.3)]{frenkel1985representations} gives the same sign convention for the irreducible ADE case.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: Twisted lattice vertices and the affine basic representation
notes: The factor \(\varepsilon_\gamma|p\rangle=\varepsilon(\gamma,p)|p\rangle\) modifies the vertex field, and its modes together with Heisenberg modes are said to give a projective current-algebra representation.
statement: For an ADE root lattice \(Q\), the space \(S(\bigoplus_{n>0}(Q\otimes\mathbb C)t^{-n})\otimes\mathbb C[Q]\), with the corrected zero-mode factors and lattice cocycle, is the level-one basic module of the untwisted affine algebra of the corresponding finite simple Lie algebra. More general momentum lattices between the root and weight lattices decompose into level-one modules by root-lattice cosets; an arbitrary even unimodular lattice is not automatically a single ADE basic module.
reconstruction: The finite ADE algebra, root lattice, level and completion conventions are specified. The result is linear for the central extension and projective for the unextended loop algebra.
fate: The original construction is \citet{frenkelkac1980basic}, published in 1980. The exact representation statement is also \citet[Theorem~2.2]{frenkel1985representations}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: The special rank-twenty-four lattice and sporadic groups
notes: A special lattice in \(\mathbb R^{24}\) is said to occur here and in finite simple groups; the number of sporadic simple groups is twenty-six.
statement: The intended lattice is the Leech lattice: up to isometry it is the unique positive-definite even unimodular rank-twenty-four lattice with no norm-two vectors. Its symmetry groups and the associated vertex constructions connect to sporadic groups and moonshine. Under the standard convention excluding the Tits group, there are twenty-six sporadic simple groups.
reconstruction: The name Leech is inferred from the rank and group-theoretic context. Its absence of roots means that the preceding norm-two-current construction alone yields no nonabelian root currents for this lattice.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1.1]{brouwerleech} states the precise lattice characterization. The maintained Atlas lists the twenty-six groups \citep{wilsonparkerbray2003sporadic}; the pre-seminar Monster-module link is identified by \citet{frenkellepowskymeurman1984natural}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: The current-algebra brackets and the omitted opposite-root case
notes: The brackets vanish for \((\gamma_1,\gamma_2)>0\), give a signed \(\gamma_1+\gamma_2\) mode for inner product \(-1\), and other relations are left unwritten.
statement: With consistent negative-exponent mode labels, lattice root currents satisfy the affine relations \[[x\otimes t^m,y\otimes t^n]=[x,y]\otimes t^{m+n}+m\delta_{m,-n}\kappa(x,y)I.\] For roots, nonnegative inner product gives commuting modes, inner product \(-1\) gives the signed sum-root mode, and opposite roots supply the Cartan mode and the central term. In the convention \([x_\alpha,x_{-\alpha}]=-\alpha\), one takes \(\kappa(x_\alpha,x_{-\alpha})=-1\).
reconstruction: The notebook gives valid partial cases but does not display the central term responsible for projectivity. Positive-exponent mode labels reverse indices and must be handled consistently.
fate: All three cases occur in \citet[equations~(1.4), (2.4), Theorem~2.2]{frenkel1985representations}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: The final DDF residue recipe
notes: Equations (26)--(30) use a null \(c\), a current with polarization \(\alpha\perp c\), and twenty-four such polarizations forming with \(c\) a basis of \(c^\perp\).
statement: Take \(c\ne0\) null in signature \((25,1)\), choose an orthonormal basis of \(c^\perp/\mathbb Rc\), and use the normal-ordered residues of the corresponding currents times \(Y_{nc}\). On a sector with the appropriate normalized value of \((c,a_0)\), these are twenty-four Heisenberg oscillators commuting with Virasoro; their classes generate the nonzero-momentum physical quotient as in record~660.
reconstruction: The omitted momentum normalization, normal ordering and orthonormal quotient basis are restored. The displayed arbitrary basis alone does not imply standard delta-normalized brackets.
fate: This repeats the construction in \citet[equations~(4)--(5) and (4.8)--(4.9)]{frenkel1985representations}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains a standard result under the stated hypotheses.

title: The blanket exclusion of ordinary Lax pairs
notes: For \(L=-\partial\bar\partial+U=-\Delta+U\), the notes say \ru{не бывает пар Лакса} and infer that \(L_t=[A,L]\) gives only Euclidean motions.
statement: This universal assertion is false without restrictions on \(U\) and \(A\). For a smooth solution of \(u_t=6uu_x-u_{xxx}\), take \(L=-\partial_x^2-\partial_y^2+u(x,t)\) and \(A=-4\partial_x^3+6u\partial_x+3u_x\). Then \(L_t=[A,L]\), including nontravelling KdV solutions. What motivates the talk is instead the richer genuinely two-dimensional fixed-energy equation \(L_t=[A,L]+BL\).
reconstruction: \ours\ The counterexample and its differential-operator check are ours, not a reported seminar intervention. The equality \(\partial\bar\partial=\Delta\) also requires the notebook normalization; with Wirtinger derivatives it equals \(\Delta/4\).
fate: The one-dimensional Lax mechanism already existed; the two-dimensional fixed-energy replacement is in \citet[pp.~245--246]{manakov1976inverse}. This is not evidence for an unrestricted no-Lax theorem.
present_status: As of November 2026: the unrestricted wording is refuted by the displayed reduction; the intended genuinely two-dimensional obstruction is not specified sufficiently to recover a theorem.

title: Counting the variables of scattering data
notes: The scattering amplitude \(S(k_1,k_2)\), with \(|k_1|=|k_2|\), has \(2n-1\) variables; at fixed energy and \(n=2\) it has two.
statement: For real positive energy \(E\), incoming and outgoing momenta belong to \(S_E^{n-1}\times S_E^{n-1}\), of dimension \(2n-2\). Allowing \(E>0\) adds one parameter. Thus the fixed-energy data in two dimensions and the potential on \(\mathbb R^2\) both depend on two real variables. For an actual scattering amplitude one must additionally impose sufficient decay and regularity, e.g. a smooth compactly supported real potential.
reconstruction: The dimension count is exact. It is not a proof of injectivity, surjectivity, or compatibility of inverse-scattering data; the notes supply none of these analytic hypotheses.
fate: The fixed-energy viewpoint precedes the talk in \citet[\S1]{dubrovinkrichevernovikov1976schrodinger}; later analytic inverse-scattering results are discussed by \citet{novikovhenkin1987dbar}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the qualifications above are essential.

title: The Manakov L-A-B triple preserves a kernel
notes: The notebook replaces \(L_t=[A,L]\) by \(L_t=[A,L]+BL\), or equivalently \(C_1L+LC_2\), and imposes \(L\psi=0\).
statement: Let \(L,A,B\) be time-dependent differential operators on a common class of smooth functions. If \(L_t=[A,L]+BL\) and \(\psi_t=A\psi\), then \(\partial_t(L\psi)=(A+B)L\psi\). Consequently the zero-energy equation is formally compatible with the evolution. At energy \(E_0\), replace every occurrence of \(L\) in the right ideal by \(L-E_0\). This is a formal compatibility assertion, not a claim that the entire spectrum is isospectral.
reconstruction: \ours\ The equation for \(\psi_t\) and the distinction between one level and the whole spectrum are supplied to make the recorded method precise.
fate: Published before the talk in \citet{manakov1976inverse}; \citet[\S4]{dubrovinkrichevernovikov1976schrodinger} gives operator identities modulo the Schrödinger operator.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; the qualifications above are essential.

title: Two-point Baker--Akhiezer data and uniqueness
notes: A genus-\(g\) curve \(\Gamma\), two marked points \(\infty_1,\infty_2\), local parameters \(w_i=k_i^{-1}\), and a degree-\(g\) pole divisor determine \(\psi\) with exponential singularities \(c_1e^{ik_1z}\), \(c_2e^{ik_2\bar z}\). The normalization is \(c_1=1\).
statement: Let \(\Gamma\) be a smooth compact connected complex curve; let the distinct marked points and the effective nonspecial degree-\(g\) divisor \(D\) be disjoint. Prescribe the two indicated exponential germs and at most the poles \(D\). For parameter values where the corresponding evaluation problem is nonspecial, the normalized Baker--Akhiezer function exists uniquely. title: The incomplete higher-genus stress-tensor formula

title: Dolbeault cohomology and the determinant of cohomology
notes: For a holomorphic line bundle \(L\) on \(X\), \(H^0=\ker\bar\partial\), \(H^1=\operatorname{coker}\bar\partial=\ker\bar\partial^+\), and \(d(X,L)=\det H^0/\det H^1\).
statement: Let \(X\) be a compact connected Riemann surface, with smooth Hermitian metrics on \(X\) and a holomorphic line bundle \(L\). Elliptic Hodge theory identifies the finite-dimensional Dolbeault cohomology with \(\ker\bar\partial_L\) and \(\ker\bar\partial_L^*\). Define \(\lambda(L)=\det H^0(X,L)\otimes\det H^1(X,L)^{-1}\). The empty top exterior power is \(\mathbb C\). The metric on the oriented surface determines its complex structure; it does not alone give a holomorphic structure on an arbitrary smooth line bundle.
reconstruction: The identifications use harmonic representatives and a specified holomorphic structure on \(L\). We fix the symbol \(\lambda\) for the notebook\textquotesingle s convention, which is dual to Quillen\textquotesingle s original determinant line.
fate: The construction predates the talk; \citet[\S\S1--2]{quillen1985determinants} uses the dual convention. \citet[\S2.2]{bost1987determinants} explicitly warns about the two conventions.

title: Line bundles of fixed degree form a Picard torsor

statement: For a fixed compact genus-\(g\) complex curve, isomorphism classes of degree-\(d\) holomorphic line bundles form \(\operatorname{Pic}^d(X)\), a complex torus torsor of dimension \(g\) under \(\operatorname{Jac}(X)=\operatorname{Pic}^0(X)\). An identification with the Jacobian requires a reference degree-\(d\) bundle; no canonical such identification exists for arbitrary \(d\).

title: Zeta regularization removes zero eigenvalues before differentiating
notes: For \(\Delta=\bar\partial^*\bar\partial\), \(\zeta_{\Delta^{\prime}}(s)=\sum_{\lambda\ne0}\lambda^{-s}\), \(\Re s>1\), and \(\det\Delta^{\prime}=e^{-\zeta^{\prime}_{\Delta^{\prime}}(0)}\).
statement: For a nonnegative elliptic Laplacian of order two on a smooth closed real two-dimensional manifold, sum the positive eigenvalues with multiplicities. The series converges for \(\Re s>1\) and extends meromorphically to \(\mathbb C\), regularly at zero. Its zeta determinant is \(\det^{\prime}\Delta=\exp[-\zeta_\Delta^{\prime}(0)]>0\). The zero eigenspace is kept separately in the determinant line, not assigned an artificial determinant factor.

title: The Quillen norm is inverted on the notebook determinant line
notes: The Hodge norm on \(d=\det H^0/\det H^1\) is multiplied by \(\sqrt{\det^{\prime}\Delta}\) in equation (7).
statement: With \(\lambda=\det H^0\otimes(\det H^1)^{-1}\), the Quillen norm is \(\|\cdot\|_{Q,\lambda}=\|\cdot\|_{L^2,\lambda}(\det^{\prime}\Delta)^{-1/2}\). Equivalently, on \(\lambda^{-1}\), which is Quillen\textquotesingle s determinant-line convention, \(\|\cdot\|_Q=\|\cdot\|_{L^2}(\det^{\prime}\Delta)^{1/2}\). Squared norms use the corresponding first powers. The corrected norm is smooth in smooth elliptic families, even across jumps of kernel dimension.

title: Finite-dimensional determinant comparison and operator variance
notes: For \(T:E_1\to E_2\), the cohomological determinant is canonically \(\det E_1/\det E_2\). In the invertible one-dimensional case \(\det T\) is then placed in \(E_1/E_2\).
statement: The determinant-of-complex isomorphism \(\det\ker T\otimes(\det\operatorname{coker}T)^{-1}\simeq\det E_1\otimes(\det E_2)^{-1}\) is canonical up to the standard consistent sign convention. Under it the induced norm is the cohomology norm divided by the product of the nonzero singular values of \(T\). In contrast, \(\det T\) itself belongs to \(\operatorname{Hom}(\det E_1,\det E_2)\), the dual line. For invertible \(T\), the canonical acyclic generator maps to \((\det T)^{-1}\).

title: Operator independence holds only in the fixed finite-dimensional model

statement: With fixed finite-dimensional Hermitian spaces, the metric on \(\det E_1\otimes(\det E_2)^{-1}\) is independent of \(T\); the isomorphism from cohomology depends on \(T\). A functorial determinant of every bare infinite-dimensional vector space, under all linear isomorphisms, is not defined by the notes.

title: The anomaly polynomial and its normalization
notes: Polyakov\textquotesingle s theorem is written \(\delta\log|\cdot|_j/\delta\rho=(6j^2-6j+1)R(\rho)\); the polynomial is called the second Bernoulli polynomial.
statement: For the Quillen metrics of \(\lambda_j=\lambda(K_X^j)\) with all bundle metrics induced from the same surface metric, conformal variation has the universal coefficient \(c_j=6j^2-6j+1\). In an explicit relative formulation, for two surface metrics \(\rho_0,\rho_1\), the ratio of Quillen norms on each fixed \(\lambda_j\) is the \(c_j\)-th power of the corresponding ratio on \(\lambda_0\). With the usual convention \(B_2(t)=t^2-t+1/6\), one has \(c_j=6B_2(j)\).

The product of relative Quillen-norm changes is \(R_0^{\sum_i b_ic_{j_i}}=1\). Thus the tensor-product norm is independent of the auxiliary smooth surface metric. title: Why thirteen and twenty-six occur
notes: The important example is \((j_1,b_1)=(2,1)\), \((j_2,b_2)=(1,-13)\); the notes infer no conformal anomaly in dimension 26.
statement: Since \(c_1=1\) and \(c_2=13\), the product \(\lambda_2\otimes\lambda_1^{-13}\) has vanishing anomaly. title: Determinant lines form a holomorphic bundle even across cohomology jumps
notes: For a holomorphic family \(X_M\to M\), the spaces \(d(X_t,\omega^j)\) are fibers of a holomorphic line bundle \(d_j\).
statement: Let \(\pi:X\to S\) be a proper holomorphic submersion with compact connected one-dimensional fibers and let \(K_{X/S}\) be its relative canonical bundle. The determinant of the perfect derived direct image \(\lambda_j=\det R\pi_*K_{X/S}^j\) is a holomorphic line bundle, with the stated fiber description and base-change compatibility. title: Belavin--Knizhnik curvature cancellation
notes: Belavin and Knizhnik\textquotesingle s theorem says the canonical metric on \(\bigotimes_i d_{j_i}^{b_i}\) has zero curvature when \(\sum_i b_ic_{j_i}=0\).

title: Zero curvature alone cannot normalize a metric
notes: Theorem (19) is said to determine the canonical metric uniquely.

title: Global constancy on moduli and the remaining scalar ambiguity
